---
title: "RADB user_ref Exploration"
code-fold: true
---

Purpose: explore RADB's `user_ref` table with a view to harmonisation.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(DBI)
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)
library(here)

here::i_am("radb-user-ref.qmd")

set.seed(123)

## Functions ##
sample_n_safe <- function(x, n) {
  x_unique <- unique(x)
  x_unique[sample.int(length(x_unique), min(n, length(x_unique)))]
}

classify_value <- function(x) {
  recode_values(x, c(NA, NULL) ~ "NA or NULL", 0 ~ "0", default = ">0")
}

read_or_write_parquet <- function(con, table_name, file_name) {
  if (!file.exists(file_name)) {
    table <- dbGetQuery(
      con,
      glue::glue("SELECT * FROM {table_name};")
    )
    nanoparquet::write_parquet(
      table,
      file_name
    )
  } else {
    table <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(
      file_name
    )
  }
  table
}

kable_abbreviate <- function(x, n) {
  table <- slice_head(x, n = n) |> knitr::kable()
  nrows <- nrow(x)
  print(table)
  if (nrows > n) {
    print(glue("\n\n*and {nrows - n} more rows*"))
  }
}

kable_glimpse <- function(x, n = 20, width = 40) {
  summary <- tibble(
    name = names(x),
    type = vapply(x, \(col) class(col)[1], character(1)),
    n_na = vapply(x, \(col) sum(is.na(col)), integer(1)),
    n_distinct = vapply(x, n_distinct, integer(1)),
    examples = vapply(
      x,
      \(col) {
        sample_n_safe(col[!is.na(col)], n) |>
          as.character() |>
          # \r escape in some comments needs to be removed
          str_replace(pattern = "\\r", replacement = "") |>
          str_trunc(width) |>
          str_flatten_comma()
      },
      character(1)
    )
  )
  cat(glue("{ncol(x)} cols x {nrow(x)} rows\n\n"))
  print(knitr::kable(summary))
}

is_double_like <- function(x) {
  x_double <- suppressWarnings(as.double(x))
  ifelse(sum(is.na(x_double)) > sum(is.na(x)), TRUE, FALSE)
}

```

# `user_ref`

```{r}
#| label: load-tables

user_ref <- read_or_write_parquet(
  con,
  "user_ref",
  here::here("data", "user_ref.parquet")
)

environmental_con <- read_or_write_parquet(
  con,
  "environmental_con",
  here::here("data", "environmental_con.parquet")
)
```

- `user_ref` is presumably the table of references for *all* data in RADB - both eData and qData
- it may be based on an existing citation format ([bibtex](https://www.bibtex.org/Format/)?), although this is not currently documented
- eData's references

```{r}
user_ref |> kable_glimpse()
```

## foreign key `environmental_con.measured_reference_id` == `user_ref.reference_id`

- As we're only interested in eData and not qData, we want to know if all eData entries correspond to a single reference
- `measured_reference_id` is stored as a character and `reference_id` as a double, which may cause issues with joining tables
- Drilling deeper into the data several issues are apparent: many entries in `environmental_con` have no `measured_reference_id`, and some `measured_reference_id` are not integers

```{r}
environmental_con |>
  count(measured_reference_id, sort = TRUE) |>
  kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- If we remove all non-numeric `measured_reference_id`, do the remaining IDs all match values of `user_ref.reference_id`?

```{r}
environmental_con_ref_id_double <- environmental_con |>
  mutate(measured_reference_id = as.double(measured_reference_id)) |>
  filter(!is.na(measured_reference_id))

anti_join(
  environmental_con_ref_id_double,
  user_ref,
  by = join_by(
    measured_reference_id == reference_id
  )
) |>
  select(
    campaign,
    environmental_con_id,
    sample_date,
    site_code,
    measured_reference_id
  ) |>
  kable_glimpse()
```

- Yes, with the exception of `measured_reference_id` == `34171643`, which corresponds to `Multisource_Test1`

- eData generates a [compact text reference ID](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/reference/generate_reference_id.html) based on the reference date, the first author's last name, and the first three words of the title (e.g. `2018Last1AStudyOf`)
- This is unlikely but technically might to generate non-unique IDs (i.e. if two papers are published the same year with the same first three title words and first author last name)
- This also has the benefit of being far more more human-friendly than an integer code

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Review use of reference ID in existing data
- Harmonise across eData/qData/RADB

**Assessment**

- Priority: 3/5
- Difficulty: 4/5
:::

# `author`

- Standard bibtex field

```{r}
user_ref |> count(author) |> kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- Inconsistent formatting in DB, sometimes contains year, title, etc.
- [eData](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/references_data.html) gets reference data from LLM or Crossref lookup, which mostly mitigates any such issues

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Add guidelines for formatting author info?
- Harmonise across eData/qData/RADB

**Assessment**

- Priority: 2/5
- Difficulty: 2/5
:::

# `publication_year`

```{r}
user_ref |>
  filter(publication_year %notin% 1940:2027) |>
  kable_glimpse()
```

- Filtered to references with "unreasonable" (i.e. not between 1940 and 2027) `publication_year`
- Appears that in some cases, this is only stored in titles (e.g. `Pascoe ea 94`)
- Recorded in eData as [References - YEAR](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/references_data.html#year), otherwise basically the same

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Check properly formatted for all references

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 1/5
:::

# `title`

- show only titles with punctuation in them, as an approximation of corrupted titles

```{r}
user_ref |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "[^\\w\\s]")) |>
  count(title) |>
  arrange(nchar(title)) |>
  kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- There are a handful of these corrupted titles in here
- Entering titles via Excel is (potentially) likely to cause more issues, as Excel will automatically use the language/location settings of the Windows user profile, which may use different encoding to RADB or the importer
- This is less likely to occur with eData/qData, as they're hosted on a specific server with specific settings. but errors may be introduced during import

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Check title formatting
- Check if import pipelines need explicit locale set

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 1/5
:::

# `doi`, `url` 

- DOIs are uncomplicated, and used identically in eData [References - DOI](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/references_data.html#doi)

```{r}
user_ref |>
  count(doi) |>
  kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- Likewise [References - URL](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/references_data.html#url)

```{r}
user_ref |>
  count(url) |>
  kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

# `reference_type`

```{r}
user_ref |>
  count(reference_type) |>
  kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- `reference_type` is always either `PRIMARY` or `REVIEW`
- Edge cases may exist (e.g. databases), but aren't anticipated to be a real issue
- No controlled vocabulary constraint appears to exist for this variable at this time
- eData's [References - REFERENCE_TYPE](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/references_data.html#reference-type) variable tracks whether the reference is a book/article/etc, akin to bibtex's [entry type](https://www.bibtex.org/Format/#entry-types)
- this is used to make various data specific to certain references conditionally mandatory (e.g. books and reports need a publisher, etc.)

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Rename eData REFERENCE_TYPE to ENTRY_TYPE for consistency with bibtex
- Extend reference_type to include `Other` category, add controlled vocabulary
- Harmonise across both

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 3/5
:::

# `series_editor`, `series_title`, `series_volume`, `number_of_volumes`, `editor_name`, `periodical_journal`, `ref_volume`, `issue`, `number_of_pages`, `ref_pages`, `epub_date`, `date_cited`, `access_date`, `ref_edition`, `publisher`, `published_date`, `published_place`, `institution`, `db_name`, `db_provider`, `accession_number`, `document_number`, `isbn_issn`, `pmcid`

- These variables exist but are almost never used:
- eData drops several of the more specific ones (`series_editor`, `series_title`, `series_volume`, `number_of_volumes`, `editor_name`, `date_cited`, `published_date`, `published_place`, `db_name`, `db_provider`, `accession_number`, `pmcid`) to reduce complexity

```{r}
user_ref |>
  select(
    series_editor,
    series_title,
    series_volume,
    number_of_volumes,
    editor_name,
    periodical_journal,
    ref_volume,
    issue,
    number_of_pages,
    ref_pages,
    epub_date,
    date_cited,
    access_date,
    ref_edition,
    publisher,
    published_date,
    published_place,
    institution,
    db_name,
    db_provider,
    accession_number,
    document_number,
    isbn_issn,
    pmcid
  ) |>
  kable_glimpse()
```



::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Identify which of the above variables capture useful metadata or could be removed?
- Consider splitting into multiple tables for different evidence types (book, database, etc) to reduce number of redundant fields

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 4/5
:::

# `entered_by`, `entered_date`

- Not currently captured by eData

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Should be added to eData for consistency across tables (based on user account?)

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 2/5
:::

# `comments`

- Set but never used
- eData has a specifically named [References - REF_COMMENT](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/references_data.html#reference-comment) field for the same purpose

```{r}
user_ref |> count(comments)
```
